name: vertex_extrude_apex_law
description: How a vertex-extrude's two settings -- the outward shift and the ring width -- interact. Eight cells on two stands, measured through the headless command lane, cross-checked against the same law read statically off the reference's own compute site.
source: Reference editor, headless command lane (two boots), plus a static read of the same kernel. No display, no pointer injection, no trace.

law.apex: The extruded apex is a NEW vertex placed at V + shift * w(V) * normalize(sum over the vertex's incident SELECTED polygons of that polygon's per-vertex normal). Its displacement magnitude is exactly `shift`; the width does not enter it. `w(V)` is the falloff weight at V and is 1 when no falloff is active -- READ but not exercised by any cell here.
law.ring: Each incident edge gains a split point at V + width * normalize(N_i - V): Euclidean distance exactly `width` from the ORIGINAL vertex position, along that edge. The shift does not enter it.
law.gates: The shift pass is gated on width > 0 AND valence >= 3. That gate is the MECHANISM behind 'shift alone does nothing' -- it is not a coincidence of the numbers, and it is why the no-op holds for either sign of shift.
law.independence: The two settings drive two separate, sequentially applied passes over the vertex. Apex and ring are therefore independent: the apex is a function of `shift` alone and the ring of `width` alone.

refuted.apex_is_shift_plus_width: REFUTED by the two reversed-ratio cells: predicts 0.4 for both, measured 0.1 and 0.3. This was the shipped hypothesis, and it was derived from the one cell that cannot tell it apart from three others.
refuted.apex_direction_is_area_weighted_normal: REFUTED on the irregular fan by 2.53 degrees -- far outside float32 noise. Indistinguishable on a cube corner.
refuted.apex_direction_is_away_from_neighbour_ce: REFUTED on the irregular fan by 77.5 degrees.
refuted.apex_direction_is_negated_mean_edge_dire: REFUTED on the irregular fan by 172.5 degrees.

cube_corner.cannot_separate: DIRECTION. At a cube corner every candidate direction rule collapses onto the outward body diagonal. A magnitude law fitted here is evidence about magnitude only.

irregular_fan_valence4.kind: closed fan of four triangles of unequal area around the origin, the centre vertex selected
irregular_fan_valence4.separates: DIRECTION. The four candidate directions are 0, 2.53, 77.5 and 172.5 degrees from the measured one.

cells.note: THE ORIGINAL CELL, and it is the degenerate one: shift == width, so 'shift', 'shift+width', '2*shift' and '2*width' all predict the same magnitude. The earlier record for this exact cell said the apex moved 0.4; re-measured here it moves 0.2.
DISCRIMINATING: shift != width and shift < width.
DISCRIMINATING: the reversed ratio. Together with the cell above this separates all four magnitude candidates.
width == 0 is a COMPLETE no-op: not one vertex moves and no topology is created, whatever the shift.
shift == 0 leaves the apex exactly where it was.
CONTROL: the same cell with the two settings applied in the opposite order, byte-identical -- so the result is a function of the pair, not of the order they were entered in.
CONTROL: doubling the width moves the ring and leaves the apex bit-identical -- the apex does not depend on the width at all.

provenance.harness: tools/local/fixture_gen/vertex_extrude/gen.py (headless command lane, two boots, isolated HOME per boot)
provenance.notes: INSTRUMENT: the headless command lane, two boots, a fresh isolated HOME each. Every apex and ring number is a MEASUREMENT of the reference, not an evaluation of a formula. The law was read independently off the reference's own compute site by static disassembly BEFORE these cells were run, and predicted them exactly, including the direction; the private toolcard records that read with its routine names and addresses. Positions come back at float32 precision, hence the 2e-6 tolerance. THIS FIXTURE CORRECTS AN EARLIER RECORD: the single prior cell (shift = width = 0.2) was reported as an apex displacement of 0.4 and shipped as a tentative 'shift + width' hypothesis; re-measured, that cell moves 0.2, and it could not have separated the candidates even had it been right.
